reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST
Indication: known MS, new left visual blurring.
Comparison: 12/27/2022.
Findings: Multiple periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintense white matter lesions. Several of these lesions show enhancement after gadolinium, indicating active demyelination. No mass effect or midline shift. No restricted diffusion. No hemorrhage. Ventricles normal in size.
reports.conclusion: Multiple periventricular white matter lesions, some enhancing, consistent with active multiple sclerosis.

documents.title: Neurology urgent visit
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - MS CLINIC (urgent slot)
Date of visit: 01/01/2024

Ms. Simard, 31, RRMS on interferon beta-1a, was seen urgently after calling our after-hours line. One year after her last relapse (left-sided sensory symptoms and right visual blurring), she now has two days of blurred vision in the left eye, an electric sensation running down her spine whenever she flexes her neck, and on-and-off numbness and tingling in the right hand for about a month.

Medications: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Left afferent pupillary defect. Visual acuity reduced on the left. Light-touch sensation diminished in the right hand. Strength, coordination, reflexes and gait otherwise as before; the remainder of the neurologic exam is normal.

Labs: CBC normal, ESR normal, B12 normal, RPR non-reactive, ANA negative.
MRI brain with and without gadolinium: multiple periventricular white matter lesions, a number of them enhancing.

Impression: Relapse of RRMS with left optic neuritis, Lhermitte phenomenon and right-hand sensory symptoms, with active lesions on MRI.

Plan: Continue interferon beta-1a. Return visit in clinic in about 6 months, earlier for any worsening of vision or new deficits.

Neurology, MS clinic

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the New Year relapse.

Read the MS clinic letter: left optic neuritis plus Lhermitte and right-hand sensory change, active lesions on MRI, staying on interferon, return in ~6 months. She says the left eye is clearing slowly, reading is easier this week. Neck zaps rare now. Right hand still a little "buzzy" at times. Missed a few days of work. Mood lower the past few weeks, PHQ-9 5; she connects it to the relapse and the dark season, no SI. Has friends nearby and is back at the gym.

Meds reviewed: interferon beta-1a TIW, oxybutynin PRN, D3 daily. Adherent, no missed injections.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Left APD noted, as in the neurology letter. Strength full. Gait normal.

A/P
1. RRMS, relapse 1/2024 with left optic neuritis; recovering. Management per neurology.
2. Mild low mood related to the relapse; PHQ-9 5. Supportive discussion; offered therapy referral, she'll think about it. Recheck at next visit.
3. Monitoring labs due in April.
4. Bladder and vitamin D unchanged.

documents.title: Monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC and LFTs normal. Sent to MS clinic. Portal message to pt.

MRI BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: MS, right eye pain and visual blurring.
Comparison: 01/01/2024.
Findings: Multiple ovoid periventricular white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities, oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles. T2 hyperintense lesions are also present within the corpus callosum. No mass effect. No acute infarct. No hemorrhage. Ventricles and extra-axial spaces normal.
reports.conclusion: Periventricular lesions perpendicular to the ventricles and corpus callosum T2 lesions, typical of multiple sclerosis.

OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - MS CLINIC
Date of visit: 07/01/2024

Seen in follow-up by a colleague of her usual MS neurologist. Ms. Simard (31) has RRMS with prior optic neuritis in each eye, most recently the left eye in January. For several weeks now the right eye has hurt, more when she moves it, and vision there has been getting blurrier, with colors looking washed out.

MRI brain (06/28): multiple periventricular lesions perpendicular to the ventricles, plus corpus callosum T2 hyperintensities.

Impression: Recurrent right optic neuritis in RRMS.

Plan: Continue interferon beta-1a. Return as needed, sooner for worsening vision.

Neurology, MS clinic

orders.reason: Neurogenic bladder with worsening urgency and leakage

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 32F.

Two relapses this year (left optic neuritis January, right optic neuritis June), both followed by the MS clinic, on interferon throughout. Vision has come back well enough to drive and work.

Main issue today is the bladder. Over the last few months the urgency hits faster and she has started leaking before she gets to the bathroom, a few times a week. Wearing a pad now. Plans errands around restrooms. Takes oxybutynin twice a day most days, not enough. No dysuria, no fever, no hematuria.

ROS otherwise negative. Mood fine, PHQ-9 3.

Exam: vitals as charted. Eyes: right APD. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no suprapubic fullness. Neuro: strength full, reflexes brisker on the left, gait normal.

A/P
1. Neurogenic bladder with worsening urgency and new urge leakage despite oxybutynin. Referral to urology for evaluation.
2. RRMS, relapses 1/2024 and 6/2024, per neurology. CBC, CMP, TSH today.
3. Vitamin D deficiency, on D3.
4. Vaccines: flu and 2024-25 COVID today. Pap 2027.
Follow-up after urology.

conditions.label: Urinary incontinence
conditions.note: Urge leakage with neurogenic detrusor overactivity.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY PRACTICE
Date of visit: 01/06/2025
Referred by: primary care, for neurogenic bladder with increasing leakage

HPI: 32-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting MS (neurology following) and known neurogenic bladder with detrusor overactivity. Her leakage has become more frequent: the loss of urine comes on abruptly with little warning, sometimes before she can get to a toilet, preceded by a rapidly building urge she cannot hold off. She has become reluctant to be away from home for long stretches. Oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily as needed gives partial relief.
Neurologic history per patient and records: several relapses with visual and sensory symptoms; brain MRIs with multiple lesions.

Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: none.
PSH: none.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks weekly, financial analyst.

Exam: Abdomen soft, no masses. Pelvic exam without masses. Lower extremities with increased tone, brisk reflexes, and reduced joint-position sense at the toes bilaterally.
Post-void residual by bladder scan: 180 mL.

Assessment: Urge urinary incontinence from neurogenic detrusor overactivity, with incomplete emptying (PVR 180 mL), in the setting of MS. Upper motor neuron signs in the legs.

Plan:
1. Clean intermittent catheterization twice daily; teaching done today with our nurse, she performed it independently. Prescription sent to a medical supply company.
2. Continue oxybutynin as currently taken.
3. Follow up in clinic as needed; call for fever or symptoms of infection.

Urology
cc: primary care

documents.title: Catheter supplies
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Supply company called, insurer wants a PCP-signed certificate of medical necessity for intermittent catheters (urology wrote the order but their form went missing). Form pulled from fax, PCP signed with urology letter attached, faxed back. Pt aware; she has a starter box from urology so no gap.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

results.text: E. coli, greater than 100,000 CFU/mL. Susceptible to ciprofloxacin.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Acute visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit, she texted this morning.

S: Two days of fever with chills and burning on urination. For the past week, more frequent and more urgent than her usual baseline. Catheterizing twice a day since urology started it in January; this is her first urinary infection. No flank or back pain, no nausea or vomiting. No new neuro symptoms. Took acetaminophen last night.

Meds: interferon beta-1a TIW, oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN, vitamin D3 2000 IU, intermittent catheters. NKDA.

O: T 38.5, BP 120/78, HR 88; rest as charted. Looks tired, not toxic. Abdomen soft and non-tender, no suprapubic tenderness to speak of. No CVA tenderness on either side.
POC urine (cath specimen): LE positive, nitrite positive. Micro: WBC >50/hpf, RBC 2/hpf, many gram-negative rods.
CBC: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250.

A/P
1. Acute cystitis with fever in a woman who self-catheterizes for neurogenic bladder. No flank pain or CVA tenderness. Treating as a complicated course given the fever and catheter use: ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x 7 days. Urine culture sent, will adjust to sensitivities. Fluids, acetaminophen for fever. Clean catheter technique reviewed; new catheter each time.
2. Go to the ED for vomiting, rigors, flank pain or fever that persists past 48 h on the antibiotic.
3. RN call in about 10 days.

documents.title: Urine culture
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Samantha, your urine culture grew E. coli and it is sensitive to the ciprofloxacin you're taking, so no change is needed. Please finish all 7 days. How is the fever?

documents.title: RE: Urine culture
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Fever broke yesterday afternoon. Still burns a little but way better.

documents.title: UTI follow-up
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt. Finished cipro on the 10th. No fever since the 4th, no burning, frequency back to her usual. Catheterizing without trouble. Reviewed when to call. Routed to PCP, problem resolved.

documents.title: Monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal. WBC back in range after April infection. Copied to neurology.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD, area hospital
Arrival 07/02/2025, 18:40

CC: right eye vision blurry, left hand jerking, peeing constantly.

HPI: 32F with RRMS, recurrent optic neuritis and neurogenic bladder (self-cath), here with symptoms she says feel like her earlier flares. Ten days ago she had a sudden sharp pain behind the right eye, then trouble focusing with that eye, worst in dim light. Since then also involuntary spasms of the left hand. Bladder: urgent trips more than 10 times a day, occasional leakage.

Meds: interferon beta-1a 44 mcg SC TIW, oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism; father with hypertension; no MS in the family.

Exam: Awake, oriented. Hyperreflexia with clonus in the left upper extremity. Vibration sense decreased in the right lower extremity. Subtle right afferent pupillary defect. Fundoscopy: mild swelling of the optic disc. Otherwise nonfocal.

MRI brain: multiple hyperintense periventricular lesions.

Assessment: MS relapse with right optic neuropathy (disc swelling), left arm corticospinal signs, bladder urgency.

Disposition: Discussed with on-call neurology by phone. Discharged home in stable condition with instructions to see her neurologist this week; return for worsening vision, weakness or retention.

Emergency medicine
Copy to PCP

documents.title: Post-ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after her ED visit on 7/2 (record received 7/7).

ED found a right optic neuropathy with mild disc swelling, left arm clonus and reduced vibration in the right leg; MRI showed periventricular lesions; sent home to see neurology. She has called the MS clinic and is waiting on an appointment date; staying on interferon in the meantime. Right eye still dim in low light. Left hand spasms less. Bladder: frequency settling back, catheterizing twice daily, no fever or dysuria.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Right APD. Strength full in all limbs, gait steady.

A/P
1. RRMS relapse 7/2025 with right optic neuropathy. Added to problem list. Neurology following.
2. Neurogenic bladder with urge incontinence on CIC + PRN oxybutynin; frequency during the flare, no infection symptoms.
3. Monitoring labs normal in May. Physical in October.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit, 33F.

Year in review: April febrile cystitis (E. coli, treated, resolved). July relapse with right optic neuropathy seen in the ED, interferon continued. Since then no new symptoms. Right eye still a touch dim at night. Catheterizing twice daily, leakage much better than last year. Oxybutynin twice daily most days.

ROS: no fever, dysuria, falls, weakness. Mood ok, PHQ-9 4.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Right APD. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Strength full, gait normal.

A/P
1. RRMS, last relapse 7/2025, on interferon beta-1a per neurology. Yearly CBC, CMP, TSH plus lipids today.
2. Neurogenic bladder with urge incontinence, on CIC and oxybutynin; no infections since April.
3. Right optic neuropathy, history of bilateral optic neuritis.
4. Vitamin D deficiency on D3.
5. Flu and 2025-26 COVID given today. Pap due 2027.
See me in spring.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD, area hospital
Arrival 12/29/2025, 14:20

CC: right leg weak and numb x2 days, left eye blurry x1 week.

HPI: 33-year-old woman with RRMS and recurrent optic neuritis in both eyes. Two days ago her right leg abruptly became weak and numb. The left eye has been blurry for a week. MS for about six years, several prior optic neuritis and sensory relapses. On interferon beta-1a since diagnosis.

Meds: interferon beta-1a SC TIW; oxybutynin 5 mg BID PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, social alcohol, financial analyst.

Exam: RLE strength 3/5 with increased tone and hyperreflexia. Left eye visual acuity decreased, with an afferent pupillary defect. Otherwise as before per patient.

Labs: WBC 7.0, Hgb 13.5, plt 250, Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 0.9, glucose 98.
MRI brain with gadolinium: multiple periventricular lesions, one enhancing.

Assessment: MS relapse with right leg weakness and left optic involvement, active lesion on MRI.

Disposition: Neurology on call contacted; patient discharged home, appointment with her MS neurologist arranged within days. Return for worsening weakness, falls or urinary retention.
